simple.meaning: קֶרַע (qeraʻ) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a rag.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 11:30. The surrounding context includes family, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קֶרַע (H7168) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Ahijah took the new garment that was on him, and tore it in twelve pieces.
